title: Taking Applications for Line Extensions and New Service Construction
content:
Member services takes **Line Extensions and New Service Construction** applications for Cedar Fork Electric Cooperative under the following rule. An application opens a construction project for one location to be served and records the member applying, the class of extension written as its official tier name, the date of the application, the service address exactly as written on the application, and the pending service account opened for the location. The project then stands in applied status.

## 1. Who and what may be taken

An application is taken only from a member where the class of extension requires membership, for a location whose new service fits one of the class's eligible rate schedules, and with a pending service account opened for the location.

| Applicant is a member (where the class requires membership) | New service fits one of the class's eligible rate schedules | Pending service account opened for the location | Application taken |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| No | Yes | Yes | No |
| Yes | No | Yes | No |
| Yes | Yes | No | No |

## 2. When engineering starts

Engineering starts once the engineering design fee has posted. The fee is billed to the project; when it posts, a staking engineer is assigned and the project moves from applied to engineering status.

## 3. What the member is told at application

The member is told at application:

- that the service entrance, weatherhead and wiring are the member's, where the class makes them the member's responsibility;
- that the cooperative supplies the meter base, where the class provides for the cooperative to supply it;
- that a member-supplied service pole is accepted only where the class allows the member to supply the service pole.

## 4. Three-phase construction and long extensions

Three-phase construction is accepted only where the class makes three-phase construction available. An extension longer than the class's longest extension built without board approval goes to the board before it is estimated.

| Proposed extension length (hypothetical, Seasonal Residence Extension, longest length without board approval 2640 ft) | Longer than that length | Goes to the board before it is estimated |
|---|---|---|
| 2,500 ft | No | No |
| 2,640 ft | No | No |
| 2,641 ft | Yes | Yes |

An extension exactly at the class's longest length is not longer than it and does not go to the board on that account.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A hypothetical member asks for a new three-phase shop service on Schedule GS-3 Three-Phase General Service. On a class whose three-phase construction is available and whose eligible rate schedules include Schedule GS-3, and with a pending service account opened for the shop, the application is taken; on a class that does not offer three-phase construction, three-phase construction is not accepted.
